inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Because there was a burning smell, this is a safety hazard' - the customer reported only a faint electrical smell and no burning.

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'almost certainly an earth-leakage fault' and 'points strongly to an internal earth-leakage fault... replace the damaged module'

rationale: The assistant correctly told the customer to stop using the hob, isolate it and get an electrician or engineer, which is the right outcome. It overstated certainty by calling this an earth-leakage fault from moisture and by saying the module needs replacing, when the cause is genuinely uncertain. It also said 'there was a burning smell', which contradicts the customer's 'faint electrical smell... no burning'. It never asked which switch trips (RCD or MCB), the key first question, and its first reply asked about other appliances instead.
